chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamili, from Abu Hashim, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves beauty and beautification, and hates misery and wretchedness.
ai.seo_question: What does Allah love and hate regarding human appearance and condition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish that physical grooming and aesthetic presentation are not merely cultural preferences but acts of worship reflecting divine attributes. This tradition counters ascetic extremes that view neglect of appearance as piety, affirming that Allah loves beauty (jamal) and dislikes wretchedness (bu's), thereby integrating spiritual purity with outward elegance. It serves as a foundational text in Shia jurisprudence for the virtue of cleanliness and proper dress as manifestations of gratitude for God's bounty.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Shuayb Al Mahamily, from Abu Hashim, from one of our companions,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Loves the beauty, and the beautification, and Hates the misery and the wretchedness’.
en.sarwar: 14. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from abu Shu’ayb al-Mahamiliy from abu Hashim from certain persons of our people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, loves beauty and beautification and dislikes misery and wretchedness.’”
